findings.description: The safety goal's timing budget does not close: 85 ms of serial work plus a 20 ms margin against a 100 ms interval.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic over FB2-SAF-SGO-000001's own timing_budget.allocation and fault_tolerant_time_interval_ms. Performed by hand, not by the validator, whose FTTI rule does not fire because it looks the interval up under a field name this record does not use.

findings.description: The contactor reaction requirement's 30 ms acceptance threshold contradicts its own 35 ms rationale and the safety goal's 40 ms allocation for the same chain.
findings.evidence: Three figures read side by side: FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 acceptance_criteria[0] threshold 30, its rationale '30 ms mechanical opening + 5 ms feedback = 35 ms', and FB2-SAF-SGO-000001's contactor_command 5 + contactor_mechanical 30 + feedback_verification 5.

findings.description: The independent monitor's justification cites a 115 ms main-path figure that appears in no record.
findings.evidence: A corpus-wide search for the literal 115 returns only this rationale and the identical text in FB2-HW-TSR-000004. The nearest real figure is the safety goal's 85 ms serial sum.

findings.description: FB2-HW-TSR-000004 and FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 are the same sentence at two ISO 26262 levels, and their shared monitoring-coverage criterion is a disjunction with an undefined term.
findings.evidence: Byte comparison of the two records' statement, rationale, safety_allocation and acceptance_criteria fields: identical in all four.

findings.description: The system requirement requires a degraded-to-fault boundary to be declared but does not supply a value for it, so it is satisfiable and not yet satisfied.
findings.evidence: The acceptance criterion 'Degraded-to-fault boundary declared, Numerical value or named rule separating degraded from fault, 1, declared value' has no corresponding value anywhere in the corpus. The record states this in its own open_point field rather than leaving a reader to discover it.
